findings.reason: the plan presents three interchangeable options of which the first cannot satisfy its own done-when, so it should either drop that option or state that it additionally requires widening the reload set in tests/mcp_family_reload.py to the other consumers.
findings.text: the deliverable's first option, "it resolves the reader from the defining module at assertion time", cannot make the done-when's pair pass: `reload_mcp_family()` reloads only `_store`, `mcp_deadlines`, `mcp_discovery`, `mcp_edit_plan` and `mcp` (tests/mcp_family_reload.py:27-31), so after the trigger `doccheck` and `roadmap` — two of the three consumers the test asserts — still hold the pre-reload function object while a live resolve reads the post-reload one; measured after `reload_mcp_family()`, `doccheck.sprint_item_slug is _store.sprint_item_slug` is False and `roadmap.sprint_item_slug is _store.sprint_item_slug` is False, while only the `__module__`/`__qualname__` comparison (both generations report `reckon._store sprint_item_slug`) passes for all three. The third option, "the reload restores the modules it replaced", does not help either: `importlib.reload` rebinds attributes to new objects and restores nothing, and widening the helper's reload set turns the live-resolve form red on all three assertions, not one — only the second option is sound as a standalone test change.
